assumptions: The cell operates 4,160 hours per year (two 8-hour shifts, five days per week, 52 weeks); actual scheduled hours may differ.
The baseline intervention rate of 6.0 per hour, measured over the frozen 312-hour baseline window, is representative of steady-state operation.
Each intervention costs $180 USD, itemized as $85 labor, $65 downtime, and $30 scrap, using customer-provided rates from the 2026 standard-cost sheet.
The 35% projected reduction is the analyst projection and lies inside the Wilson 95% CI [18.64%, 52.18%] computed from 9 of 27 matched failure events.
Maintaining the improvement requires 22 engineering hours per month at a loaded rate of $95 per hour (monitoring, re-verification, data pulls).
The projection applies only to the four failure taxonomy labels present in the baseline window; failure modes absent from the window are out of scope.
Scrap cost assumes 2026 material prices provided by the customer; a change of 10% or more in material prices invalidates the scrap line item.
